title: ValIdation of Symptom and self-management InformatiON in Inflammatory Bowel Disease – A Real-World Observational Study Using a Patient-Centric Data Collection Approach
summary:
Chronic inflammatory bowel diseases such as Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis often occur in phases and can greatly affect a person’s quality of life. Many patients have to manage symptoms, uncertainty, and emotional strain in their daily lives. Digital tools may help people better understand their condition and support them in coping with it.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether a smartphone application can help patients manage their condition more effectively, improve their quality of life, and increase their knowledge about the disease.

Participants will use a specially developed application over a period of about one year. They will regularly provide information about their well-being, symptoms, and daily life. In addition, information from routine medical care will be included. The collected data will be analyzed to better understand how the use of the application relates to disease course and well-being.

interventions.name: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) use a digital self-management application ("CED Buddy") as part of routine care. Patient-reported outcomes (PROMIS, IBD Disk, PRO2, IBD-KNOW), app usage data, and clinical routine data (e.g., CRP, fecal calprotectin, medication) are collected prospectiv

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis)
Possession of a compatible smartphone and willingness to use the app regularly
Ability and willingness to provide written informed consent
Ongoing care at one of the participating study sites
Exclusion criteria:
Severe cognitive, psychiatric, or physical impairment preventing meaningful participation or app use
Participation in an interventional study that may interfere with study outcomes
Acute severe disease flare at baseline (defined as need for intravenous corticosteroids or hospitalization within the past 30 days)
Active severe infections (e.g., tuberculosis, sepsis, cytomegalovirus, listeriosis, or opportunistic infections such as progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy)
